question: Do neighbouring source frames show coherent landmark/edge displacement or observation loss at the 025 diagnostic selections?
scope: BOI only; three awake sources, six contiguous clips containing 68 original frames plus one first-frame reference per source (71 unique source frames). The clips are review context, not analysis windows.
selection: 025 flagged indices plus five neighbours on either side; overlapping ID402 503/505 intervals merged. ROIs chosen from already viewed 025 source sheets before loading the new sequences; not blinded.
coordinates: ROIs are [first column, first row, width, height] in native one-based pixels; fixed across each recording. Three visible vessel/perimeter locations per recording, used only as visual landmarks, not tissue masks.
display: Fixed recording ranges inherited from 021/025; no frame normalization, temporal averaging, registration, source warping or smoothing. Native 96x96 crops displayed at integer enlargement; full frames preserved.
interpretation: Look for coherent landmark/edge displacement across locations and continuity before/after selected frames. Brightness or texture changes alone cannot identify motion. Weak evidence stays unresolved; no numeric acceptance threshold.
stop: One extraction and fixed-ROI review. No adaptive crop or display tuning to obtain an exclusion. If inconclusive, retain uncertainty and state what additional evidence would resolve it.

completion.remaining: Measurement-specific support/exposure decisions, uncertain boundaries and fine-motion limitations; no further registration tuning implied.
